_about: State-wise legal awareness. Each item: jurisdiction (central law vs state), statutory provisions resolved at display time against the official bare-act library (the text shown is the statute, not a paraphrase), official links with the date they were checked, and FAQs that point to the provisions. General information only — not legal advice. To add a state: add an entry under 'states' and items with that state code.

items.subject: licence
items.title: When you need a driving licence
items.summary: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a central law and applies in every state. It requires a person driving a motor vehicle in a public place to hold an effective driving licence for that class of vehicle, sets minimum ages, and makes it an offence for an owner to let an unlicensed person drive. Licences are applied for and renewed through the Sarathi portal of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

faqs.q: Can I drive with only a learner's licence?
faqs.a: Learner's licences carry conditions; read Sections 3 and 4 and the conditions printed on the learner's licence. The Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 set the learner conditions — confirm them on Sarathi.

faqs.q: How long is my licence valid?
faqs.a: Validity depends on the licence type and your age — see Section 14 shown here.

items.subject: registration
items.title: Registration of motor vehicles
items.summary: A motor vehicle may not be driven in a public place unless it is registered and the certificate of registration is in force. Registration is applied for to the registering authority (in Maharashtra, the Regional / Sub-Regional Transport Office) and most services are online on the Vahan portal. Drivers must produce the licence and certificate of registration on demand by an authorised officer.

faqs.q: Must I carry the original documents?
faqs.a: Section 130 requires production of the licence and certificate of registration on demand; whether a digital copy is accepted depends on the rules and government notifications in force — confirm on Parivahan/DigiLocker before relying on it.

items.subject: road_safety
items.title: Helmets, seat belts, speed and drunk driving
items.summary: The Act requires protective headgear for persons on motorcycles (with stated exceptions), safety belts, observance of speed limits, and forbids driving dangerously or under the influence of alcohol or drugs. The penalties are set out in the penal sections shown below — open each one for the current text, because amounts were revised by amendment.

links.title: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (official)

faqs.q: Is a helmet compulsory for the pillion rider?
faqs.a: Read Section 129 shown here: it applies to every person driving or riding on a motorcycle, subject to the exceptions it states.

items.subject: challan
items.title: Traffic challans: paying, contesting and court disposal
items.summary: Many traffic offences can be compounded (settled by paying the compounding amount) under Section 200. If you dispute a challan you can decline to compound, in which case it goes to court; petty traffic cases may be disposed of summarily under Section 208, and many states route e-challans to online Virtual Courts. Challans issued through the national e-challan system can be checked and paid on the Parivahan e-challan portal.

faqs.q: What if I think the challan is wrong?
faqs.a: Do not pay a compounding amount you dispute. You may contest it before the court (or Virtual Court) handling the challan; keep evidence such as photographs, receipts or location records.

faqs.q: Can the police keep my licence?
faqs.a: Section 206 sets out when an officer may impound documents — read the text shown here.

items.subject: challan
items.title: Paying or contesting e-challans in Maharashtra
items.summary: Maharashtra Traffic Police issue e-challans that can be viewed and paid on the Maharashtra traffic e-challan payment portal; challans in the national system can also be checked on Parivahan. Mumbai Traffic Police publish their own services. Disputed challans are decided by the court or Virtual Court — see the central provisions on compounding and summary disposal.

faqs.a: Use the portal named on your challan (the challan number shows which system issued it). Do not pay through unofficial websites or links received by SMS without checking the domain.

items.subject: accidents
items.title: Compensation after a road accident
items.summary: Claims for compensation arising out of motor accidents are decided by Motor Accident Claims Tribunals. The Act sets out who may apply and where. Report the accident to the police, keep the FIR / accident report, medical records and bills, and check the limitation and procedure in the provisions shown.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to file a claim?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but claims involve evidence of negligence, injury and income; legal aid may be available through the District Legal Services Authority.

items.subject: state_services
items.title: Maharashtra public services online (Aaple Sarkar)
items.summary: The Government of Maharashtra delivers many certificates and services online through the Aaple Sarkar portal, and transport services through the Transport Department and Parivahan portals. Service timelines and fees are notified by the State — check the service page before applying.

items.subject: state_services
items.title: State amendments and transport notifications (Maharashtra)
items.summary: States make their own motor vehicle rules and issue notifications (for example on fees, compounding amounts or local restrictions). NyaySutra has no verified Maharashtra notification on record yet, so none is summarised here — consult the Transport Department's official notifications before advising on a state-specific point.
